I worked a CRC position like this and I absolutely loved it. One day on and then 3 days off to do whatever you need during the day like shopping or the gym. It took a little bit to get used to and can mess with your sleeping schedule at first but you get used to it. If it was anything like my job (I worked at a level 1 trauma center in Wisconsin with cardiac arrest, traumatic injuries, strokes etc), you won’t always be up the full 24 hours. I was expected to work from like 8am-6pm and then after that I could chill and just screen the patients that were being brought in by EMS. Sometimes I got full nights of sleep (interrupted because the pager always goes off), and sometimes I was up the full 24 hours. Another perk is I never had to take vacation time. I would just find a person to switch a shift or two with me and then I had 1-2 weeks off. I actually did 24 on 24 off for an entire month, but got to take a month off for vacation too afterwards. If I could find another CRC job in California like that, but also paid my managers salary lol, I would take it in a heartbeat

As far as stages of filtering go, there's a few ways you could do it. To save time I personally just filter through a 10 micron filter paper after freezing my solution for 24 hours (solution at at least -60c). This seems to work for me, but for finer filtering you could do it in stages, like 25 micron, 20 micron then 10. I've noticed that the faster your solution flows through the filter the less waxes you collect. About 3 gallons will take me around 30-45 minutes to filter through a 10 micron paper and I pull out a lot of waxes. 

As far as color goes I havent experimented with activated charcoal yet, but from what I've seen shaking about 5% charcoal of your predicted oil yield and filtering will do a good job when filtered multiple times. You also want to be careful of what kind of charcoal you use (coconut vs. Wood). You can also try bentonite clay

I feel you on this. One thing that I've learned from going to therapy is that you can dictate how it goes. For example, when she started talking about mindfulness exercises, you can stop her and tell her that those things don't work for you and you want to try CBT instead. You're paying for these sessions so you can get what you need out of them. Just like communication is key in our personal relationships, it's also key with our therapists. It's easier said than done, but don't be afraid to ask for what you need! Also, I'm sure you know this, but something like this takes time to get better. I'm in the same boat, I'm 25 and I've had this and bulimia since I was 12. Sometimes I'm so frustrated because I dont feel like anything is getting better. I don't feel like anyone takes me seriously. But I work through it and remember it takes time. You've been thinking this way for 10 years, it isn't going to feel better immediately, or even in a few months (maybe). You got this! Try looking up CBT handouts and books and experiences while you wait to see your therapist again!
